title: Robust self-test of the maximally entangled state of two-qubits without assuming unitary observables
abstract: Standard device-independent self-testing uses Naimark dilation to assume projective measurements, masking the operational limitations of realistic non-unitary observables. We establish a robust pure self-test for the singlet and Pauli observables that entirely circumvents dilation of the measurement apparatus. Assuming a pure state to model an untrusted source, we regularize the physical non-projective operators and derive an analytic $\mathcal{O}(\sqrtε)$ robustness bound. Our results suggest that device-independent certification of real implementations is significantly more demanding than standard projective models imply.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous theoretical framework to self-test maximally entangled states without assuming that local measurements are perfectly projective. By regularizing general POVMs and deriving an $O(\sqrt{\epsilon})$ robustness bound, the authors show that real-world measurement imperfections impose stricter limitations on entanglement certification than previously thought.
main_problem: To develop a robust self-testing protocol for entangled quantum states that accurately accounts for non-projective, realistic local measurements, bypassing the limitations of standard methods relying on Naimark dilation.
main_result: The authors derive an analytic robustness bound scaling as $O(\sqrt{\epsilon})$ for certifying entanglement using general POVMs, showing that real experimental constraints impose a significantly higher cost than idealized projective models suggest.
method: They regularize physical non-projective operators using a modified sign function and decompose the total error into terms related to regularization ($\Delta$) and standard unitaries (funitaries), bounding both analytically.
model_or_system: The study focuses on certifying the maximally entangled two-qubit singlet state using local measurements $\{A_x\}$ and $\{B_y\}$, modeled by general binary POVMs, rather than assuming ideal projective measurements.
key_observables: CHSH Bell operator expectation value ($\langle B angle$), local measurement probabilities $p(a, b|x, y)$, and the error parameter $\epsilon$.
important_parameters: The robustness bound scales as $O(\sqrt{\epsilon})$, where $\epsilon$ quantifies the deviation from ideal entanglement.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption challenged is that local observables must be strictly projective (unitary); the work explicitly circumvents Naimark dilation by regularizing operators instead.
paper_structure: The paper establishes a framework to test entanglement robustly, first addressing the failure of standard methods due to non-projective measurements. It then introduces regularization techniques and derives an analytic bound on the total error ($\Delta + 	ext{funitaries}$) based on the measured Bell violation $\epsilon$.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial refinement for device-independent quantum information protocols, offering a more physically accurate assessment of entanglement certification when measurement apparatuses are imperfect or non-ideal.
